avalancheActivity.comment: Hazardous areas are mainly found on high-altitude, very steep, shaded slopes. Furthermore, as altitude increases, small patches of drift snow are prone to instability, particularly on ridges and passes, as well as in wind-blown gullies and hollows. Small to medium-sized snow slab avalanches triggered by winter sports enthusiasts are possible. Activities away from secured slopes require experience in terrain and avalanche assessment.
avalancheActivity.highlights: Take particular care on high, steep, shaded slopes

snowpackStructure.comment: The precipitation over the past few days has already resulted in a continuous snow cover at higher altitudes. With strong winds at times, fresh drifts of wind-blown snow have formed, particularly on ridges and mountain passes. Some of these drifts are prone to instability. Fresh snow and drift snow lie, particularly on steep, shaded slopes, partly on top of accumulated, angular crystals. The Avalanche Warning Service still has very little information from the terrain as a whole.

tendency.highlights: It will remain dry, but temperatures will rise significantly. As temperatures rise, small to medium-sized snow slides are possible on steep, smooth slopes.

weatherForecast.comment: On Saturday, the sun will shine unclouded over the mountains and temperatures will rise significantly. At mid-altitudes around 1,000 metres, there will be patchy, persistent fog on the slopes. Temperatures at 2,000 m will rise from -7 to 0 degrees, and at 3,000 m from -12 to -4 degrees. High-altitude winds: light to moderate, blowing from the north-east to the east
